papers.name: Papers 1 to 4 (all content: Breadth in biology and Depth in biology, Foundation 01/02, Higher 03/04)

topics.name: Chapter B1 You and your genes
points: B1.1 Nucleus and genetic material of eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells; using a light microscope to observe plant and animal cells (PAG1)
B1.1 The genome; DNA as a double-helix polymer of nucleotides; genome and environment influence phenotype
B1.1 Chromosome, gene, allele, variant, genotype and phenotype; the genome as instructions for ordering amino acids in proteins
B1.1 DNA nucleotides (sugar, phosphate, base); triplet code; protein synthesis with mRNA and ribosomes (triple)
B1.1 Variants arise from mutations; effects of variants in coding and non-coding DNA on phenotype (triple)
B1.2 Gamete, homozygous, heterozygous, dominant, recessive; single gene inheritance and genetic diagrams
B1.2 Predicting outcomes of single gene crosses using ratios and probability; most features are controlled by multiple genes
B1.2 Development of understanding of genetics from Mendel to genome sequencing (triple)
B1.2 Sex determination in humans and the role of genes on the Y chromosome (triple)
B1.3 Importance of genome understanding for medicine: disease alleles and genetic testing
B1.3 Genetic engineering: isolating and replicating genes, vectors, inserting genes, selecting modified cells
B1.3 Benefits, risks and ethical considerations of gene technology in agriculture and medicine

topics.name: Chapter B2 Keeping healthy
points: B2.1 Health and disease; communicable and non-communicable disease; how pathogens (viruses, bacteria, protists, fungi) spread
B2.1 Human infections (influenza, Salmonella, athlete's foot, malaria, HIV/AIDS) and plant diseases (TMV, ash dieback, crown gall)
B2.2 Non-specific human defences against pathogens; platelets
B2.2 The human immune system and adaptations of white blood cells
B2.2 Physical and chemical plant defences against pathogens (triple)
B2.3 Reducing and preventing the spread of communicable diseases in animals and plants
B2.3 How vaccines prevent disease and the need for high vaccination coverage
B2.4 Detecting and identifying disease; observing microorganisms with a light microscope (triple, PAG1)
B2.4 Aseptic technique and culturing microorganisms; calculating areas of clear zones using πr² (triple, PAG7)
B2.4 Production of monoclonal antibodies and their use in diagnostic tests (triple)
B2.5 Genetic and lifestyle risk factors for non-communicable disease; effect of exercise on pulse rate (PAG6)
B2.5 Interpreting data on non-communicable disease: sampling, frequency tables, histograms, correlation; interactions between diseases
B2.6 Medicines including antibiotics; calculating clear zones of antibiotic action (PAG7)
B2.6 Treatments for cardiovascular disease: lifestyle, medicines and surgery
B2.6 Discovery and development of new medicines: preclinical and clinical testing
B2.6 Monoclonal antibodies in treating cancer (triple)

topics.name: Chapter B3 Living together – food and ecosystems
points: B3.1 Photosynthesis: inputs, outputs, endothermic reaction, role of chloroplasts; investigating requirements and products (PAG5)
B3.1 Enzyme action: active site, specificity, effects of substrate concentration, temperature and pH (PAG4)
B3.1 Effects of temperature, light intensity and CO₂ on rate of photosynthesis; limiting factors; inverse square law (PAG5)
B3.2 Substances moved into and out of producers; diffusion, osmosis and active transport (PAG8)
B3.2 Partially permeable membranes; water and mineral ion uptake by root hair cells
B3.2 Structure of xylem and phloem; transpiration, translocation and stomata (PAG1)
B3.2 Using a potometer; effects of light, air movement and temperature on water uptake (PAG6)
B3.3 Synthesis and breakdown of biological molecules; qualitative tests for biological molecules (PAG2)
B3.3 Producers, levels of organisation in an ecosystem; interdependence and competition
B3.3 Trophic levels, pyramids of biomass and efficiency of biomass transfer (triple)
B3.3 Carbon and water cycles and the role of microorganisms in cycling substances
B3.3 Effects of temperature, water and oxygen on rate of decomposition; calculating rate of decay (triple)
B3.4 Abiotic and biotic factors affecting communities
B3.4 Field investigation of distribution and abundance; estimating population size (PAG3)

topics.name: Chapter B4 Using food and controlling growth
points: B4.1 Aerobic and anaerobic respiration: conditions, inputs, outputs and ATP yields; respiration as exothermic and continuous
B4.1 Mitochondria and respiration; effect of different substrates on rate of respiration in yeast (PAG5)
B4.2 Electron microscopy and sub-cellular structures; size, scale and standard form in the context of cells
B4.3 The cell cycle and mitosis; observing stages of mitosis with a light microscope (PAG1); cancer
B4.3 Meiosis and the formation of gametes
B4.3 Stem cells in embryos and adults, meristems in plants; cell differentiation by switching genes on and off
B4.4 Plant hormones: auxins in phototropism and gravitropism (PAG6) (triple)
B4.4 Gibberellins and ethene; uses of plant hormones to control plant growth (triple)
B4.5 Benefits, risks and ethical issues of using stem cells in medicine

topics.name: Chapter B5 The human body – staying alive
points: B5.1 Substances moved into and out of the body; animal cell membranes and diffusion, osmosis and active transport
B5.1 The circulatory system; structure and function of the heart
B5.1 Arteries, veins and capillaries; red blood cells and plasma
B5.1 Surface area to volume ratio and the need for exchange surfaces and transport systems
B5.2 Components of the nervous system; structure of neurons and synapses
B5.2 The reflex arc; investigating reflex actions (PAG6)
B5.2 Structure and function of the brain; difficulties of investigating brain function (triple)
B5.3 The endocrine system; thyroxine (negative feedback) and adrenaline
B5.4 Maintaining a constant internal environment; the skin and temperature control (PAG6)
B5.4 Body responses to temperature challenges: receptors, processing, effectors and feedback (triple)
B5.4 Osmotic challenges, the kidneys and ADH in water balance (triple)
B5.5 Hormones in the menstrual cycle: FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone
B5.5 Hormonal and non-hormonal contraception; hormones in treating infertility
B5.6 Insulin and glucagon in control of blood sugar; type 1 and type 2 diabetes
B5.6 Structure and function of the eye; pupil response (PAG6)
B5.6 Eye defects and their correction; limitations of treating brain and nervous system damage (triple)

topics.name: Chapter B6 Life on Earth – past, present and future
points: B6.1 Genetic variation and mutation; natural selection and competition; evolution and speciation
B6.1 Selective breeding of food plants and domesticated animals
B6.1 Evidence for evolution: fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria
B6.1 The work of Darwin and Wallace and the impact of their ideas on biology and society (triple)
B6.2 Advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction (triple)
B6.3 Classification and how developments including DNA analysis have changed it
B6.4 Human interactions with ecosystems and their effects on biodiversity; maintaining local and global biodiversity
B6.4 Environmental change and the distribution of organisms (triple)
B6.4 Food security and biotechnological and agricultural solutions including genetic modification (triple)

topics.name: Chapter B7 Ideas about Science
points: IaS1 Planning investigations: hypotheses, apparatus, variables, sample size, risk and communicating methods
IaS2 Presenting data: units, significant figures, graphs and lines of best fit
IaS2 Analysing and evaluating data: means, ranges, outliers, accuracy, precision, repeatability, conclusions
IaS3 Correlation and cause; how explanations develop over time; peer review; using models
IaS4 Applications, risks and benefits of science and technology; ethical issues; communicating science

topics.name: Chapter B8 Practical skills
points: PAG1 Microscopy and PAG2 Testing for biological molecules
PAG3 Sampling techniques and PAG4 Rates of enzyme-controlled reactions
PAG5 Photosynthesis and PAG6 Physiology, responses and respiration
PAG7 Microbiological techniques and PAG8 Transport in and out of cells
